record.paper_title: Time and Norm Optimal Controls: A Survey of Recent Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: Consider the self-adjoint setting discussed in the paper: A is a self-adjoint infinitesimal generator in a separable Hilbert space, H_α = D((μI - A)^α), and a control is called regular when its multiplier z belongs to Z(T) and strongly regular when z belongs to E*. Is it true in this self-adjoint setting that whenever an optimal control reaches a target ȳ satisfying ȳ ∈ D(A), the associated multiplier must actually satisfy z ∈ E*? Equivalently, does regularity imply strong regularity in the borderline case α = 1 of the smoothness relation between the target and the costate?

evidence.quote: Significantly, the proof of Part (a) of Theorem 4.1 excludes the case α = 1, where the implication would be ȳ ∈ D(A) => z ∈ E or, equivalently, regular => strongly regular. Whether this implication holds in the present self adjoint setting seems to be an open problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let H be a separable complex Hilbert space and let A: D(A) ⊂ H → H be a self-adjoint infinitesimal generator of a strongly continuous semigroup {S(t)}_{t≥0} on H. Fix μ ∈ ℝ such that μI − A is positive and self-adjoint, and for α ≥ 0 define the scale of Hilbert spaces H_α = D((μI − A)^α) endowed with the graph norm ‖x‖_α = ‖(μI − A)^α x‖. Set H_{−α} to be the completion of H with respect to ‖x‖_{−α} = ‖(μI − A)^{−α} x‖, so that (H_α)* ≅ H_{−α}.

Consider the linear control system
   y'(t) = A y(t) + B u(t),  t ∈ [0, T],   y(0) = y_0,
with admissible controls u ∈ L^∞(0, T; U) (U a Hilbert space) and a bounded control operator B: U → H. For a fixed target ȳ ∈ H, an admissible control u is called norm/time optimal if it achieves ȳ at time T while minimizing the corresponding cost. To any optimal control u there is associated, via the Pontryagin maximum principle, a "multiplier" (costate) z, characterised through the dual semigroup; this z lies a priori in a space of distributions on [0,T] taking values in an extrapolation space.

Let Z(T) denote the space of admissible multipliers (those z for which the maximum principle pairing ⟨B^* S(T−t)^* z, u(t)⟩ is well defined for all admissible u), and let E* ⊂ Z(T) denote the subspace of "strongly regular" multipliers (those z for which the costate trajectory t ↦ S(T−t)^* z takes values in the dual H_{−1}^* ≅ H_1, equivalently z is associated to an element in the natural energy space).

Call an optimal control regular if its multiplier z belongs to Z(T), and strongly regular if z ∈ E*.

Question. Suppose A is self-adjoint as above. If an optimal control reaches a target ȳ with ȳ ∈ D(A), must its associated multiplier z satisfy z ∈ E*? Equivalently, in the borderline case α = 1 of the smoothness correspondence between target and costate, does regularity imply strong regularity?
artifact.status_search_result: No specific resolution of this borderline α = 1 implication (regular ⇒ strongly regular under self-adjoint A with target in D(A)) was located in standard searches; it is described as an open problem in the surrounding literature on time- and norm-optimal control, and no later work clearly settling it was identified.

status_evidence.title: Time and Norm Optimal Controls: A Survey of Recent Results and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Whether this implication holds in the present self adjoint setting seems to be an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The implication regular ⇒ strongly regular at α = 1 in the self-adjoint setting is stated as open.
